_comment: PRIOR ART: scripts/analysis/cluster-books.py — clusters whole books, not passages about one person. One entry per figure: prefix = the full-text prefix searched in pages_en (prefix*); name = the regex that names him in a sentence; out = where the page data is published; minCluster/minSamples = HDBSCAN settings for the theme map (about passages/250, floor 10). setAside = passages whose book title matches `titles` and text matches `text` (both default to anything), and whose text does not match `unless`, are given a fixed theme before clustering: they name someone else, or the figure as a fictional speaker. rare = settings for rare.py: skipTitles/skipText drop passages that are about someone else, notes attach a sentence where a passage means something other than it seems.

setAside.why: Philolaus as a speaker in Reuchlin's dialogue De arte cabalistica (1517), reprinted with Galatinus and Pico
Philolaus, a companion of Apollonius in Philostratus, not the Pythagorean

rare.skipText: thebes|theban|lawgiver|nomothet|of corinth|Philolaus,\s*(prepare|it depends|let us|surely|I beg|yesterday|we will)|laws by which|patrimon

notes.match: boulliau|bullial|antiphilola|philolaus reborn|philolaus restored|motion of the heart
notes.note: Ismaël Boulliau published a book of his own titled Philolaus (1639), arguing that the earth moves; this passage is about that book, not the ancient Philolaus.
This is Philolaus the younger, a speaker in Johann Reuchlin’s dialogue On the Art of the Kabbalah (1517).

setAside.why: Archytas of Amphissa, the poet Athenaeus quotes on apples

notes.note: Plutarch tells this of Archimedes, not Archytas; the book has swapped the names.
